text:
Sean Couturier is the Flyers' captain, a former Selke winner, and the man who supplied the line of their road trip after the overtime loss in Calgary: Flyers "finding ways to lose", in NBC Sports Philadelphia's headline. He'd had two assists that night. It's been that kind of season for him: one goal and seven points in 20 games, and his ice time is down 1:19 a night over the last ten.

The defending is still the reason he plays. Evolving-Hockey had him taking 0.17 expected goals per 60 away from opponents last season, 96th percentile among forwards, and he kills penalties. But Philadelphia takes only 42% of the expected goals at five on five with him on the ice, which is about the team's share overall: he isn't dragging them down, and he isn't lifting them either. His shooting (4.5% this season, against about 12% for him) will improve. At 33, on a team in Philadelphia's spot, the bigger question is what his role looks like in a year.
